parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized that test15.py must become pure Node ESM .mjs code in /output, with four required CLI options, byte-exact base58 encode/decode output, no external modules, and no Buffer or Uint8Array interface.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It used two workflows: an early probe workflow to characterize Python behavior and a later adversarial breaker workflow. The parent retained implementation ownership and wrote the final files.
parallel.implementation: The parent built a multi-module base58 port with argparse, bytes repr, traceback, linecache, unicode, and print helpers, then kept modifying traceback and source-line behavior near the deadline.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final artifact contained test15.mjs and a lib tree under /output; status artifact validation marked the directory copy and expected entry as present.
parallel.verification: The run used child probes, local comparison harnesses, and an adversarial breaker workflow. A breaker result reported concrete stream/exit-status divergences, but the parent did not incorporate it before timeout.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The agent was killed by the timeout after a local probe/edit command. Official evaluation completed afterward and failed with 67/102 samples despite a present artifact.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same pure Node ESM, manual argv, base58 behavior, Python bytes repr, traceback, and output placement requirements without using delegation.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One parent owned the full pipeline: probing the executable, writing modules, building a comparison harness, running differential checks, and revising the implementation.
serial.implementation: It wrote test15.mjs plus local base58, argparse, bytes-repr, traceback, linecache, unicode, and error helpers, then tuned behavior against local differential tests.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact also contained the expected test15.mjs entry and local library modules under /output, with artifact validation succeeding.
serial.verification: It ran local comparison harnesses from /workspace and /workspace/dataset, both reaching 171/171 matched cases before a longer fuzz command was killed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial process also reached the task timeout and official evaluation failed 67/102, leaving no pass/fail advantage over the parallel run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the ESM .mjs, manual argv, byte-exact output, local-only import, and no Buffer/Uint8Array-interface requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received and worked from the same prompt requirements for the same base58 migration task.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is proven; both attempted the same broad behavioral parity task.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split behavior discovery and adversarial checking into workflows while the parent retained final implementation and edits.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no delegation and kept probing, implementation, and verification in one parent trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete difference is parallel delegation for research/verification versus a single local owner in serial; ownership itself was not missing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children were briefed as behavioral probes and a breaker; the important returned interface was a workflow journal with concrete divergences.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept findings inside one local context and directly reran compare.mjs after changes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The critical context difference is lifecycle use of returned verifier evidence, not an absent child brief or missing cross-agent API contract.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented a richer module hierarchy and was still editing traceback/linecache behavior near the end.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a flatter module set and used compare.mjs to align normal argv, bytes-repr, decode, and traceback behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both built plausible ports; parallel had external verifier findings about abnormal stream and exit-status cases that were not integrated before shutdown.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel launched an adversarial workflow in the background and had a completed result with specific divergences available in its journal.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not have child results; its verification results were immediate local command outputs in the parent trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel failed to consume an available child verifier result, while serial had no comparable handoff boundary to miss.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delivered an /output tree with test15.mjs and multiple local helper modules; no write collision or overwrite episode is proven.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial delivered an /output tree with test15.mjs and local helper modules; no shared-agent state existed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The two artifacts differ in module organization, but the evidence does not show a concurrency write conflict causing the failed score.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used both local probes and workflow verification, but the breaker identified concrete stdout, stderr, and exit-status divergences that were not acted on.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran local compare.mjs checks that matched 171/171 cases in two working directories before broader fuzz was killed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had stronger adversarial child feedback but worse result lifecycle use; serial had only local verification and no child handoff omission.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used two workflow calls, 33 child logs, and the full 2399-second agent window before returncode 143.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial disabled workflows, used no subagents, and also consumed the full 2399-second agent window before returncode 143.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both timed out and both officially failed; parallel spent much more coordination budget but the retained adverse consequence is specific nonuse of a completed result.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome. The current completed status.json evaluation gives both modes 67/102 and solution_passed false. The task-solving difference is process-level: parallel used workflows and left a completed adversarial verifier result unconsumed, while serial worked locally and achieved the same official score after local 171/171 harness checks before timeout.
parallel_contributors: Workflow delegation produced additional adversarial findings, but the parent did not use the completed breaker result before closure.
serial_contributors: Single-agent local comparison kept verification findings in the same context, but the run still timed out and failed the same official evaluator count.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both final artifacts passed 67/102, so unresolved edge-case behavior remains in both attempts; the official score does not isolate one unique coding defect from the logs alone.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is an adverse parallel process consequence only

The parent launched an adversarial verifier workflow, received a completed workflow result with concrete stdout, stderr, and exit-code divergences, but did not inspect or apply that result before continuing local traceback/linecache edits and then timing out. The adverse consequence is unconsumed verifier evidence and a shortened correction window, not a pass/fail split because both runs failed 67/102.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parallel parent left concrete adversarial verifier findings unincorporated while spending the remaining window on local probes and edits, so the run ended with unresolved known divergence reports and no completed whole-task closure.
candidates.near_match_reason: The verifier finding was not trapped below a child; it was present in the parent-visible workflow journal and the workflow launch message explicitly told the parent where to inspect cached completed results.
